Lydia / Ethan —

Attached is a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP) focused on the capacity reservation and onramp for your Dedicated + Private deployment. High level: we want to minimize go-live risk by staggering a reserved GPU pool (Dedicated) for steady production traffic and an on-prem procurement pathway for Private deployments with acceptance milestones aligned to your QA window.

Key asks from Aurora for this draft: please confirm acceptance criteria for performance (p95 latency < 300ms token generation for the inference path you care about), a target production date for the pilot, and any procurement lead constraints on your side (preferred vendors / long-lead PO windows).

Highlights in the attached workbook (aurora_map_v2.xlsx):
- Phase A: evaluation sprint (2 weeks) — model compatibility + sample load tests on hosted instances. Owner: Aurora + Redwood SE.
- Phase B: Dedicated reservation (initial pool) — billing commit + 8–12 week provisioning runway. Owner: Redwood sales/capacity.
- Phase C: Private on-prem procurement — hardware lead 10–16 weeks (dependent on vendor). Owner: Aurora procurement + Redwood solutions.
- Contingency: burst capacity + hybrid routing for first 6 weeks of pilot.

I’ve looped in Ben for sizing/lead time details and Jordan for commercial sequencing. Can we sync tomorrow 30 minutes to align on acceptance criteria and procurement milestones?

Thanks,

Lydia — quick technical breakdown and proposed hedging approach. TL;DR: 8–12w for Dedicated baseline is realistic for reserved GPU pools on cloud partners for H100-class instances; Private (on-prem) procurement typically 10–16w from order to rack. We recommend a hybrid hedge: reserve a minimal committed pool (40% of expected steady-state) + short-term burst capacity and a progressive top-up schedule.

Sizing (starter assumptions from your pilot inputs):
- Target peak sustained QPS: 60 QPS
- Average token generation per request: 1,200 tokens
- Concurrency target: 10 sessions concurrently generating
- Estimated tokens/sec: (60 requests * 1200 tokens) / 1 sec = 72k tokens/sec peak (note: generation spreads over a few seconds per request; this is a conservative peak estimate)
- Benchmark throughput per H100-like GPU (quantized runtime, batch tuning): ~8k–12k tokens/sec depending on model/sequence length and quantization profile

Estimate GPUs needed (conservative): 72k / 9k = ~8 GPUs (recommend starting with 10 GPUs committed to allow headroom for validation + minor traffic spikes). If you use model distillation/quantization aggressively we can target 6–7 GPUs.

Lead-time considerations and hedges: 
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved): 8–12w provisioning — we can front-load a 4–6 GPU reserve while the remaining GPUs are phased in.
- Burst/hybrid: we can configure automatic overflow to hosted pool for up to +50% capacity for first 8 weeks (billing as usage overage) — this covers ramp risk.
- Private on-prem: vendor lead often driven by H100 board availability; plan 10–16w. Consider a parallel procurement of staging nodes (smaller config) for acceptance testing to avoid delaying QA.

Acceptance gating recommendations:
1) Eval load test on hosted sandbox (week 0–2): target p95 < 350ms for 512 token sample;
2) Pre-commit validation (week 3–4): dry-run on committed Dedicated pool with synthetic load;
3) Final acceptance (week 6–8): production pilot with routing rules and fallback verified.

I’ve attached a quick sizing sheet (gpu_sizing_estimate.xlsx) with the math and three band scenarios (conservative / expected / optimized). Happy to walk through on the call.

— Ben Carter

Mutual Action Plan (condensed):
- Week 0 (Aug 4–10): Evaluation sprint (hosted sandbox). Owner: Aurora Eng + Redwood SE. Deliverable: compatibility test results; pass/fail per test matrix.
- Week 2–4 (Aug 11–31): Pre-commit validation on a starter Dedicated pool (4–6 GPUs). Owner: Redwood capacity + Ben. Deliverable: synthetic load report; DocuSign SOW placeholder created.
- Week 4–8 (Sep 1–28): Commit tranche 1 (top-up to 10 GPUs). Owner: Aurora procurement + Redwood sales. Deliverable: PO accepted; config and routing in place; pilot cutover plan.
- Week 8–16 (Sep 29–Oct 27): Private procurement & staggered on-prem delivery. Owner: Aurora procurement + Redwood solutions. Deliverable: acceptance hardware onsite (staging for cutover).
- Contingency: 8 weeks of burst routing to hosted pool post-cutover. Owner: Redwood runtime operations.

Sign-offs / Gates:
- Gate A: Eval pass (Aurora Eng sign-off)
- Gate B: Performance verification on starter Dedicated pool (Aurora product + Redwood SE)
- Gate C: PO & billing commit (Aurora procurement + Redwood sales)

Action items (short):

- Aurora procurement: initial PO intent email with vendor constraints (Due Aug 11).
- Redwood: provide final SOW + DocuSign by Aug 14; create starter Dedicated pool by Aug 18.

I’ll upload the final MAP workbook (aurora_map_final.xlsx) with the table and DocuSign link. If this looks good we’ll convert these checkpoints into milestone rows in the HubSpot deal and set reminders.
